ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the lines AB and CD intersect at point O, $\angle EOC = 90^\circ$, OF is the angle bisector of $\angle AOE$, $\angle COF = 34^\circ$. What is the degree measure of $\angle BOD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\angle EOC=90^\circ$ and $\angle COF=34^\circ$, \\
it follows that $\angle EOF=56^\circ$,\\
since OF is the angle bisector of $\angle AOE$,\\
it follows that $\angle AOF=\angle EOF=56^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle AOC=\angle AOF-\angle COF=22^\circ$,\\
hence $\angle BOD=\angle AOC=\boxed{22^\circ}$.

Point O also emits two rays OF and OE, where the order of the rays in the upper half from left to right can be regarded as OA, OC, OF, OE, OB, and F is located inside ∠EOC, and C is located inside ∠AOF.
Reasoning: It is known that ∠EOC = 90°, ∠COF = 34°. Because F is inside ∠EOC, ∠EOF = 90° − 34° = 56°. Also because OF is the angle bisector of ∠AOE, ∠AOF = ∠EOF = 56°. In the figure, C is located between A and F, therefore ∠AOC = ∠AOF − ∠COF = 56° − 34° = 22°. Since AB and CD intersect, ∠AOC and ∠BOD are vertical angles, so ∠BOD = ∠AOC = 22°.
